_comment: MLA prefill shapes for gfx950. Two regimes, tagged per shape by the 'regime' key -- see _regime_note. Covers DeepSeek V2/V3/V3.1/R1 (Hq=128) and Kimi-K2 (Hq=64). Canonical MLA geometry: qk_nope=128, qk_rope=64, v_head_dim=128, kv_lora_rank=512, q_lora_rank=1536, Hkv=1. block_size=16. fp8 variants included for the Phase 2 fp8 bench (gfx950+ only; see DESIGN.md S6 dtype plan).
_regime_note: Every shape carries a 'regime' key: 'full_prompt' (seqlen_q == seqlen_k) or 'chunked' (seqlen_q << seqlen_k). DESIGN.md S2.5 defines two prefill strategies split at seqlen_q ~200 -- in-loop latent expansion (S3 kernel) below, materialize K/V then standard flash (S3.1) above -- and S9 rows 1-4 scope both plus the dispatch between them. The full_prompt family alone measures only the materialize side: every one of its shapes has seqlen_q = seqlen_k >= 512, so the S3 kernel is never measured in the regime it exists for. An earlier revision of this file shipped only that family. The chunked family is what brackets the threshold (seqlen_q 128 below it, 256 just above, 512 well above), what makes seqlen_q != seqlen_k at all (the cu_seqlens_k path of S3, unexercised by a square mask), and what tests S2.5's 1/seqlen_q prediction that materialize degrades as the chunk shrinks against a fixed context. Report the two families separately; a full_prompt number is not evidence about the chunked regime. If the two strategies land within noise across the whole chunked family, S2.5's two-branch dispatch is unjustified -- record that and amend the design rather than shipping a dispatch between equivalents. The chunked entries are bf16 only, for the same reason the batched ones are (see _batch_note): fp8 is Phase 2 and crossing the axes would double a set that is already specification rather than runnable input.
_dtype_note: The fp8_e4m3 entries are Phase 2 (see DESIGN.md S6 dtype plan); Phase 1 is bf16 only. The existing prefill harnesses (benchmark_prefill2d_live.py, both arches) do not read this field at all: they load ndjson UAShape records via _ua_shape_utils.load_shapes and key dtype off the torch dtype strings q_dtype/k_dtype, with is_fp8 = ('float8' in shape.k_dtype); filter_prefill_2d drops non-bf16/fp16 shapes rather than defaulting them. This 'dtype' key is metadata for a future MLA runner. Do NOT run the fp8 entries against a bf16/fp16 harness and read the result as an fp8 number.
_harness_note: These shapes are a specification for a future MLA runner, not runnable input for the current one. The existing prefill harness loads ndjson UAShape records via _ua_shape_utils.load_shapes, not this nested-object JSON, so it parses zero shapes from this file and does so silently (undecodable lines are skipped). It also requires a per-shape 'head_size', which MLA has no single value for: d_nope+d_rope=192 for the score, d_V=128 for the output. Wiring MLA shapes into a runner is part of the kernel deliverable (DESIGN.md S9).
_batch_note: The batch axis here is deliberately narrower than the decode files' B in {1,4,8,32}, and it is measuring a different thing. Decode needs batch because the pre-step is batch-invariant while the flash loop is not, so the two crossovers of DESIGN.md S4 only appear across B. Prefill has no such BATCH crossover -- its seqlen_q crossover is S2.5's, swept on the seqlen_q axis of the chunked family (see _regime_note), not on this one: its pre-kernel amortizes over total_q = batch * seqlen_q, so batch and seqlen_q are interchangeable for it and a uniform-length batch sweep re-measures points the seqlen sweep already covers, at multiplied cost. What batch does buy at prefill is coverage of the packed-varlen path -- cu_seqlens_q/cu_seqlens_k prefix sums and the per-sequence causal mask -- which B=1 exercises only trivially. Hence B=4 at the two short lengths, where that coverage is cheapest, and B=1 above. The batched entries are bf16 only: fp8 is Phase 2, and crossing the two axes would double a set that is already specification rather than runnable input. Mixed sequence lengths within a batch are the case that most needs covering and this schema cannot express them; that belongs with the runner work (DESIGN.md S9).

models._note: Hq=64 (differs from DeepSeek Hq=128); all other MLA geometry is identical.
